title: Special Systems: No Solution and Infinitely Many Solutions
description: Recognize parallel and overlapping lines, then use sliders, slope-intercept form, and proportions to find constants that create no solution or infinitely many solutions.

questions.stem_html: The system \(y=4x+3\) and \(y=mx+5\) has no solution. What is m?
questions.explanation_html: The intercepts differ, so the lines must be parallel. Equal slopes require m = 4.
questions.variation: Equal slopes and different intercepts for a parameterized line

questions.stem_html: The system \(2x+y=11\) and \(6x+3y=c\) has infinitely many solutions. What is c?
questions.explanation_html: The second left side is exactly 3 times the first. Multiply the right side by the same factor to make the lines coincide, giving c = 33.
questions.variation: Make one equation a complete multiple of the other

questions.stem_html: The system \(4x+y=9\) and \(ux+4y=v\) has infinitely many solutions. What is \(u+v\)?
questions.explanation_html: Multiply the entire first equation by 4. The second equation then has u = 16 and v = 36, so u + v = 52.
questions.variation: Determine two constants for overlapping lines

questions.stem_html: The system \(3x+by=c\) and \(6x+7y=10\) has infinitely many solutions. What is \(c/b\)?
questions.explanation_html: The equations describe the same line. The ratio of right side to the y coefficient is preserved, so c/b = \(\frac{10}{7}\).
questions.variation: Read a constant ratio without solving each constant first

questions.stem_html: The system \(5x+y=11\) and \(px+4y=48\) has no solution. What is p?
questions.explanation_html: Match the slopes by making the second left side 4 times the first. That requires p = 20. The constant on the right is 48 rather than 44, so the lines are distinct.
questions.variation: Make coefficients proportional while retaining different constants
